column1: # sdk/SOURCES.tsv -- the upstream releases sdk/usr/include is assembled from.
#   <repo>  TAB  <tag>  TAB  <licence>  TAB  <what it supplies here>
# Tags are PINNED and never tracked as a branch: docs/SDK_SURVEY.md §6.2 found
# the published trees drift both ahead of and behind any given Xcode SDK, so a
# silent upstream bump is exactly the failure mode that would produce a mystery
# six months from now.  Every one of these is a public release at
# https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/<repo>/releases/tag/<tag>.
# All four licences below permit redistribution, which is why sdk/usr/include
# is committed rather than fetched at build time.

column1: # The libmalloc pin is the one that is not "newest", and the reason is worth
# writing down because docs/SDK_SURVEY.md §6.2 predicted exactly this shape of
# problem. In libmalloc-792 and later, malloc_zone_malloc_options_t moved from
# Apple-internal SPI into the PUBLIC malloc/malloc.h. vendor/objc4-priv/
# hand-declares that enum -- it had to, because the SDK objc4 was ported
# against did not have it -- so staging libmalloc-812 gives objc4 the same
# enumerators twice and objc-runtime-new.mm stops compiling:
#   vendor/objc4-priv/malloc_private.h:7:5: error: redefinition of enumerator
#       'MALLOC_ZONE_MALLOC_OPTION_NONE'
# libmalloc-715.140.5 is the last release before the move, and is the same
# generation as the SDK the objc4 port was measured against. Pinning it also
# closes the survey's other libmalloc note: malloc/_malloc_type.h was 77%
# line-identical to the 15.4 SDK because the published revision had run ahead.
# The alternative -- teaching vendor/objc4-priv/malloc_private.h to stand down
# when the public header already declares the enum -- is not available: it is
# an enum, so there is no macro to test with #ifdef.
